text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa to propose Nenad Porges to president Tudjman as the new economy minister.
- Some 50,000 expatriates expected to return to Croatia by year 2002, assistant immigration ministar Nikola Vidak says in an interview.
- Dubrovnik may become a golf mecca if talks with British hotel magnate Rocco Forte on building of a $35 million golf course in the area succeed.
- The government plans to launch a crackdown on black marketeers in order to enforce order in trade and raise its tax revenue.
- Possible changes to the driving school procedures: Future motorists will have to drive at least 1,000 kilometers as opposed to the current 250 to be able to take a driver's test.
- Raiffeisenbank Croatia still seeking to buy shares in coffee, tea and snacks producer Franck at 150 percent of face value.
- New environmental strategy proposal for the coastal area envisages closure of all but "clean industry" along the Adriatic.
- PM Zlatko Matesa reminds new head of the oil company INA that its prices are still at the same level they were at before the world price fell to $18.47 from $24 per barrel.
- Zagreb had a 29 million kuna budget surplus in 1996 on total revenues of 2.2 billion. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
